title: NYT Reports Trump Paid $750 in Federal Income Tax
description_short: The New York Times reported Trump paid $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and 2017.
description_medium: The New York Times reported that Donald Trump paid $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and again in 2017, while claiming large business losses. The figures drew attention because they contrasted with the wealth and success he publicly projected. The reporting raised questions about how his finances were structured and what his tax records revealed.
description_long: A New York Times investigation published in September 2020 reported that Donald Trump paid $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and another $750 in 2017, while his tax records showed large losses. The contrast between those reported payments and his public image as a wealthy, successful businessman intensified scrutiny of his finances. The report relied on tax information obtained by the newspaper; the linked record here summarizes its central finding but does not provide the underlying returns or a detailed account of every deduction, business loss, or tax strategy. The reported amount is evidence of what the newspaper found in those two years, not by itself a determination that a crime occurred. The episode became part of a broader debate about the complexity of the tax code, the ability of high-income taxpayers to offset income, and whether voters should have access to a presidential candidate’s financial records. The supplied source link now leads to a Times account-help page, so this description stays within the stated figures and does not add unsupported specifics about the calculation.

The regulation narrowed the definition of waters covered by federal Clean Water Act protections, reducing the set of waterways subject to federal jurisdiction under the rule. That boundary matters because it helps determine where federal permits and pollution controls apply, and where oversight may instead depend on state or local authorities.
